extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR facilities, state permitting authorities, and regulatory stakeholders (industry, attorneys, environmental reviewers)
extracted.subtask_short: CCR management unit definition and scope
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble guidance and final-rule criteria defining what constitutes a CCR management unit (CCRMU), which units are included or excluded, the tonnage thresholds that trigger monitoring/corrective-action/closure requirements, and related procedural expectations for identification and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of CCR management unit (CCRMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed to define a CCR management unit or CCRMU as any area of land on which any non-containerized accumulations of CCR are received, placed, or otherwise managed, that is not a CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is based on existing definitions of CCR pile and CCR surface impoundment, relying on the concept of “accumulations of CCR.” EPA intended the definition to capture solid waste management practices that, per risk assessments and damage cases, have the potential to contaminate groundwater. EPA noted the proposed definition was broad but did not intend that placement of any amount of CCR would necessarily constitute a CCRMU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of units/activities included as CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: CCRMU would include historical solid waste management units such as CCR landfills and surface impoundments that closed prior to October 19, 2015, inactive CCR landfills (including abandoned piles), structural fill sites, CCR placed below currently regulated CCR units, evaporation ponds, or secondary or tertiary finishing ponds that have not been properly cleaned up, and haul roads made of CCR if the use does not meet the definition of beneficial use in §257.53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explained these examples involve direct placement of CCR on the land in sufficient quantities to raise concern about releases of hazardous constituents and generally lack measures to effectively limit contact between CCR and liquids and leachate generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed that the following would not be considered CCRMU: closed or inactive process water ponds, cooling water ponds, wastewater treatment ponds, and stormwater holding ponds or aeration ponds; areas managing exclusively non-CCR waste; and containerized CCR such as silos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These units are not designed to hold accumulations of CCR and generally do not contain significant CCR. EPA also noted CCR used in roadbed and associated embankments would generally not be considered CCRMU because methods of application differ and available risk information cannot be extrapolated, although exceptions apply if roadbed CCR is contaminating groundwater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for full CCRMU requirements (1,000 tons)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is revising §257.50(d) to specify that part 257, subpart D applies to CCRMU of 1,000 tons or greater, located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundwater monitoring, corrective action, closure, and post-closure requirements apply only to CCRMU containing at least 1,000 tons of CCR. This threshold was incorporated consistent with the results of EPA's risk analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of smaller CCRMU (1 to <1,000 tons) — FER-only until permitting determination
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR management units greater than or equal to 1 ton and less than 1,000 tons, located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit, are only subject to the requirements of the facility evaluation report (FER) in §257.75 until a permitting authority determines that regulation of these units, either individually or in the aggregate, is warranted and determines the applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA deferred regulation of these smaller units to permitting authorities to assess risks individually and/or in the aggregate and determine appropriate requirements. Facilities must identify these smaller units as part of the FER so permitting authorities have the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirement for accumulations (records or visual evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed that facilities would only be required to identify accumulations if records confirm the existence of the CCRMU or visual evidence of CCR placement on the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA emphasized that the proposed measures are not expected to identify truly de minimis quantities of CCR and that identification relies on facility records or visible on-the-ground evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inactive CCR landfill
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed to define 'inactive CCR landfill' to mean an area of land or an excavation that contains CCR but that no longer receives CCR on or after the effective date of this final rule and that is not a surface impoundment, an underground injection well, a salt dome formation, a salt bed formation, an underground or surface coal mine or a cave. For purposes of this subpart, this term also includes sand and gravel pits that received CCR and abandoned CCR piles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies which former disposal areas are treated as inactive CCR landfills subject to the rule's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCRMU located beneath critical infrastructure — deferred closure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule defers the requirement to initiate closure where the CCRMU is located beneath critical infrastructure (e.g., high power electric transmission towers, air pollution control or wastewater treatment systems, or an electrical substation) until the infrastructure is no longer needed, a permit authority determines closure is necessary, or the closure/decommissioning of the facility, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical exception to immediate closure obligations where closure would disrupt critical facility operations, subject to later action or permitting authority determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: If CCR in roadbed is contaminating groundwater, must address it
rubrics_metrics.description: Although EPA considers available information does not demonstrate that use in roadbed presents sufficient risk to warrant the suite of CCRMU requirements, that calculus changes if the CCR in roadbed is contaminating groundwater. If a facility subsequently determines the roadbed is contributing to contamination, it would be required to address that contamination as part of ongoing remediation of the aquifer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA gave example that during corrective action, identification of roadbed as an additional contamination source requires addressing it as part of remediation. Thus placement method alone does not preclude remediation obligations if contamination is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to facilities with regulated CCR unit or active facility without regulated unit
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to CCRMU of 1,000 tons or greater located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA limited application to facilities that have other regulated CCR units or are active facilities without a regulated CCR unit, rather than applying broadly to any land with CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA's reliance on risk assessments and damage cases to justify regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA stated the CCRMU regulated under the final rule are those demonstrated in the 2014 and 2024 Risk Assessments and the damage cases to have the potential to contaminate groundwater, and that the record documents CCRMU present risks at least as significant as units regulated under 2015 rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA used modeling (including quantities from 1 ton to 78,000 tons) and sensitivity analyses showing potential GWPS exceedances (up to 40×) and radiation risks under certain future land uses to support thresholds and the decision to regulate. EPA modeled individual placements, noted aggregate risk from multiple small placements could be greater, and could not identify a precise amount between 1 and 1,000 tons below which there is no reasonable probability of adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory basis and authority citations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA asserts the requirements to regulate CCRMU fall within authority delegated in RCRA sections 1008(a)(3), 4004(a), and 4005(d), and that the rule does not expand scope beyond what Congress envisioned; the 2016 WIIN Act amendments reaffirm EPA's authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble addresses major-questions arguments and explains Congress left the term 'CCR unit' to EPA to define, and that extension to inactive units consistent with statutory language on 'disposal' and 'open dump' is supported by precedent and statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-specific corrective action (not facility-wide cleanup akin to Subtitle C §3004(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule requires CCR facilities to remediate only the contamination associated with the disposal of CCR on-site of a facility with other currently regulated CCR disposal units and imposes the same unit-specific obligations applicable since 2015, not a cleanup of any Appendix IV constituent from any on-site source unrelated to CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA contrasts this with Subtitle C facility-wide corrective action obligations, clarifying the scope is unit-specific and limited to CCR-related contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify CCRMU ≥1 ton as part of FER to support permitting
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires facilities to identify CCRMU between 1 and 1,000 tons as part of the facility evaluation report so that permitting authorities have information to assess whether regulation is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports permitting authorities' ability to evaluate both individual and aggregate risks from smaller CCRMU when making regulatory determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification in §257.50(d) — scope language
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA codified the scope in §257.50(d): (1) This subpart applies to CCRMU of 1,000 tons or greater located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit; (2) CCRMU ≥1 ton and <1,000 tons located at such facilities are subject only to FER requirements until a permitting authority determines otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the regulatory text implementing the policies discussed in the preamble and establishes the bright-line tonnage thresholds and FER-only treatment for smaller units pending permitting review.
